open_obligations: Check that Parrish et al. (2022a) give judges a 5-minute limit on QuALITY as the target record states
Decide whether the single-turn study (Parrish et al., 2022b, 2204.05212v2), cited in the same marker, should get a parallel link

Note the setting difference: Parrish et al. set a limit of 5 minutes per judgment, from pilot response times, so that judges have adequate time to consider all the arguments and text snippets; Bowman et al. ask participants to answer under a 5-minute limit so that they cannot read the story in full and must rely on the model to gather relevant information
out.other_title: Judging protocol: first and second judgments, top-half pilot judges, 5-minute limit
out.rationale: Bowman et al. ask human participants to answer QuALITY questions under a 5-minute time limit, roughly paralleling Pang et al. (2022) and Parrish et al. (2022a,b), which prevents them from reading the story in full and forces them to rely on the model to gather relevant information. Parrish et al.'s two-turn study sets a limit of 5 minutes per judgment, from the pilot response times of its high-performing judges, so that judges have adequate time to consider all the arguments and text snippets. The passages show a parallel design choice made for different purposes, not Bowman et al. building on Parrish et al.'s judging protocol, and the target is a judging-protocol method that states no question or claim that Bowman et al. bear on; neither record bears on the other's claim, so the link proposes only SHARES_TOPIC for the shared 5-minute design choice.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: 5-minute time limits for human participants on QuALITY questions; holds as a shared design choice only, since the limit is set per judgment of arguments in Parrish et al. and caps answering questions with model assistance in Bowman et al.

text: To create a challenging QuALITY task that requires model assistance, the authors give participants a 5-minute time limit, roughly paralleling Pang et al. (2022) and Parrish et al. (2022a,b). This prevents them from reading the roughly 5,000-word story in full and forces them to rely on the model to gather relevant information.
